campaigns.name: 6-Minute Funnel
campaigns.objective: signups — drive self-serve signups by making the time-to-value claim concrete and verifiable
campaigns.big_idea: Post a Show HN where the builder live-installs funnelscope on a real SaaS demo app and shares the working funnel screenshot in the thread. The mechanic is radical transparency: show the exact steps, the exact time, and let HN readers poke holes. This mirrors the Plausible DNA of stating trade-offs honestly and letting outcomes speak.
campaigns.hook: Show HN: I built a funnel tool that goes from snippet install to first working funnel in 6 minutes — no tracking plan, no SQL

sample_copy.headline: From snippet to funnel in 6 minutes. No SQL. No tracking plan.
sample_copy.body: funnelscope auto-captures events from a lightweight snippet. You point at UI elements to define steps — no instrumentation project required. All data stays on EU servers (Frankfurt) with a signed DPA available. We measured the median time-to-first-funnel across our beta cohort: 6 minutes. Here is the install walkthrough. Tell me where it breaks.
sample_copy.cta: Try the free tier — up to 50k events/month, no card required

assets_needed: Screen-recorded walkthrough of snippet install to first funnel (under 6 minutes)
Screenshot of a working funnel from the demo app
Written Show HN post with honest trade-offs section
campaigns.success_metric: Number of new workspace signups in the 72 hours after the HN post
campaigns.why_on_brand: Mirrors the DNA's 'state trade-offs honestly' and 'let outcomes speak' principles; uses the verified 6-minute proof point directly

campaigns.name: Investor Update Deadline
campaigns.objective: awareness — reach founders at the exact moment they realize they don't know their activation numbers
campaigns.big_idea: A short, plainspoken Reddit post in r/SaaS and r/startups framed as a question: 'What do you tell investors when you don't actually know where signups drop off?' The post shares the honest problem, not a pitch, and links to funnelscope only in a comment if asked. The mechanic is community candor, not promotion.
campaigns.hook: What do you tell investors when you don't actually know where signups drop off?

sample_copy.headline: Preparing an investor update and realizing you have no funnel data is a specific kind of panic.
sample_copy.body: We built funnelscope for exactly that moment. Auto-captured events, point-and-click funnel steps, no analytics engineer needed. EU-hosted by default — not as an enterprise add-on. 312 workspaces are in beta now. Free up to 50k events/month. If you've been in that investor-update panic, I'd like to hear how you handled it.
sample_copy.cta: Free beta signup in the comments if you want to try it

assets_needed: Follow-up comment with signup link and honest scope description
List of 3-5 subreddits where ICP founders are active
campaigns.success_metric: Upvotes and direct replies asking for the link within 48 hours
campaigns.why_on_brand: Candid, no-jargon framing; honest about the specific pain; no vague superlatives — consistent with the DNA's 'willing to state what the product is NOT good for' style

campaigns.name: EU by Default
campaigns.objective: awareness — reach GDPR-conscious founders who are evaluating analytics tools on privacy grounds
campaigns.big_idea: A LinkedIn post series (3 posts, one per week) that explains what EU data residency actually means in practice for a SaaS founder — signed DPA, Frankfurt servers, no consent banner required for analytics. Each post is educational, not promotional. funnelscope is mentioned as the context, not the subject.
campaigns.hook: EU data residency for analytics: what it actually means vs. what vendors usually mean

sample_copy.headline: 'EU-hosted' means different things depending on who's saying it.
sample_copy.body: For funnelscope it means: data processed and stored in Frankfurt, signed DPA available on request, no data routed through US infrastructure. We made it the default — not an enterprise add-on. If you're a SaaS founder selling to European customers, your analytics tool is part of your GDPR story. Worth knowing what you're actually signing up for.
sample_copy.cta: Free tier available — see the DPA before you decide

assets_needed: One-page plain-language DPA summary to link or screenshot
Simple diagram showing data flow (EU only)
campaigns.success_metric: Profile visits and inbound DMs from founders asking about the DPA within the campaign window
campaigns.why_on_brand: Leads with privacy and EU hosting as accountability mechanisms, not just selling points — directly mirrors the DNA's 'do' list

campaigns.name: No Analytics Engineer
campaigns.objective: signups — convert founders who have Mixpanel or Amplitude installed but unused
campaigns.big_idea: A Product Hunt launch positioned explicitly as the analytics tool for teams without a data hire. The tagline and first comment both acknowledge what funnelscope does NOT do (no raw SQL export, no custom dashboards) to filter for the right users. Honest scoping is the differentiator.
campaigns.hook: Product analytics for the team that hasn't hired a data person yet — and probably won't for a while

sample_copy.headline: funnelscope: working funnels without an analytics engineer
sample_copy.body: Auto-captured events. Point-and-click funnel steps. No SQL, no tracking plan, no instrumentation sprint. EU-hosted by default with a signed DPA. Built for 2-15 person SaaS teams who need to answer 'where do signups drop off' before the next investor call — not for teams who need a full data warehouse. Free up to 50k events/month.
sample_copy.cta: Try the free tier — 312 teams are already in beta

assets_needed: Product Hunt listing copy and tagline
Product screenshots showing point-and-click funnel builder
First comment with honest scope (what it does and does not do)
Short demo GIF of snippet install to first funnel
campaigns.success_metric: Number of upvotes and new workspace signups on launch day

campaigns.name: Changelog as Content
campaigns.objective: retention — keep beta users engaged and turn weekly changelog posts into a public trust signal
campaigns.big_idea: Publish the weekly changelog as a short, plainspoken newsletter pitch to indie-founder and SaaS newsletters (e.g. Indie Hackers digest, TLDR Founders). Each entry is one concrete thing that shipped, one honest thing that is still broken, and one question for readers. The mechanic is building in public without the performance.
campaigns.hook: What shipped in funnelscope this week — and what we know is still broken

sample_copy.headline: Week N: what shipped, what broke, what we're not sure about yet
sample_copy.body: This week: point-and-click funnel steps now work on single-page apps without page reloads. Still broken: funnel step reordering loses your filter settings — fix is in review. Not sure yet: whether auto-capture should include form field values by default (privacy trade-off). 312 workspaces in beta. Free tier is open. Tell us what you'd fix first.
sample_copy.cta: Follow the changelog or join the free beta

assets_needed: List of 5-8 newsletters and communities to pitch
Short pitch email to newsletter editors
campaigns.success_metric: Newsletter reply rate and new signups attributed to changelog posts over 4 weeks
campaigns.why_on_brand: Transparent, candid, willing to name what is not working — the DNA's 'principled' and 'understated' tone applied to building in public

confidence.notes: BRAND_DNA is from Plausible Analytics, not funnelscope itself — voice and principles are borrowed by analogy as instructed. All proof points used (312 workspaces, 6-minute median, EU Frankfurt) come from APP_PROFILE.proof_points. No numeric claims were invented. No named customers or testimonials were used.
